item.description:
Cam Skattebo NYG Running Back

Hughes makes clear that he thinks Skattebo’s time as the clear-cut lead back is over, recapping coach John Harbaugh’s offseason attempts to acquire a bellcow, while noting that Skattebo is currently in the doghouse. Hughes believes Skattebo is a nice complementary player who can function as a physical change-of-pace option. The biggest issue the Giants face in replacing him is cost. He thinks a player like Jonathan Taylor will cost a Day 2 pick, at least, and he is not sure Taylor is worth that, given the Giants’ long-term plans for the 2027 draft capital they’ve accrued via various personnel moves. Trading away Kayvon Thibodeaux is an option, but doing so is challenging with Brian Burns (knee) out for the year.

Source: SNY TV

item.title: Lamar Jackson (ankle) practiced on Thursday.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

After a weird limited session on Wednesday where he wasn’t out in front of the media, Jackson practiced today in full view of reporters, who noted that he was not favoring his ankle at all. Jackson’s injury has always felt tenuous, but even if Wednesday was sort of an aberration, he has to at least be considered to be moving towards playing. Friday’s status will tell the rest of the story. He was officially limited again today. We expect him to at least be questionable after practicing the first two days of the week.

Source: Jamison Hensley

item.title: Breece Hall (quad) returned to practice on Thursday.
item.description:
Breece Hall NYJ Running Back

Reporters on the scene said that Hall headed to the rehab area after reporters left the scene, so he’ll probably be given a limited session. Still, he moved well and likely at least has a chance to suit up for Week 7 after this update. Friday’s practice will be telling. It would be surprising if Hall doesn’t at least hit the questionable line as long as he practices on Friday.

Source: Brian Costello

item.title: SNY TV’s Connor Hughes believes the Giants will stick with J.J. McCarthy as the starter “for the foreseeable future.”
item.description:
J.J. McCarthy NYG Quarterback

According to Hughes, “this is the player they targeted and wanted” as their quarterback the minute Jaxson Dart (knee) got hurt. Hughes acknowledges that coach John Harbaugh could eventually bench McCarthy later in the year, but it will take more than a bad “game or two” for that to happen. In the meantime, the weekly fantasy football outlooks for Malik Nabers and Isaiah Likely are more volatile than they were with Jameis Winston at the helm. Selling high could make sense. Hughes adds that McCarthy would have to play like a top-10 quarterback to make the coaching staff consider him for the starting role next season. That outcome seems highly unlikely.

Source: SNY TV

item.title: ESPN’s Adam Schefter reports that Elijah Arroyo will undergo shoulder surgery and miss the rest of the 2026 season.
item.description:
Elijah Arroyo SEA Tight End

Arroyo will have multiple injured reserve stints on his NFL record by the time his third season begins next year. Arroyo has caught 16-of-26 targets for 196 yards and one touchdown in regular season play thus far in his career. The talented receiving tight end fell in the 2025 NFL Draft due to knee-related health concerns. Hopefully, a strong offseason propels him to career-best figures in 2027.

Source: Adam Schefter

item.title: Seahawks activated Zach Charbonnet (knee) from the reserve/physically unable to perform list.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

Charbonnet underwent ACL reconstruction after suffering his season-ending knee injury in the Seahawks’ Divisional Round win over the 49ers. He will make his 2026 debut in Week 7 against the Chiefs, facing his former teammate, Kenneth Walker. Charbonnet’s expected workload is unknown, though he could handle enough touches to be FLEX-viable. As long as he stays healthy, Charbonnet should advance to the RB2 ranks in the coming weeks.

Source: Gregg Bell

item.title: Baker Mayfield said his injured thumb has “gotten to a place where it’s strong enough to play” in Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield has played through injuries regularly over the years. We expect him to be out there for the Buccaneers’ Week 7 game against the division rival Panthers. He is a QB2 for his first game back. A run-heavy game plan could be in the works as they ease him in. If his thumb really is good to go, though, this game could turn into a shootout. He practiced in full for the second time this week on Thursday, and told reporters that he will play with a protective plate on the back of his glove to help prevent re-injury.

Source: Greg Auman

item.title: Andrew Thomas (groin) resumed practicing on Thursday.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Thomas, the team’s left tackle, RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and backup OT Marcus Mbow (knee) are “all on the practice field participating to some degree in position drills during the media viewing period,” per USA Today’s Art Stapleton. This is good news for the Giants’ offense as a whole.

Source: Art Stapleton

item.title: NBC Houston’s Aaron Wilson reports that David Montgomery (groin) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Giants.
item.description:
David Montgomery HOU Running Back

Like we said yesterday, Montgomery is still seemingly in the week-to-week camp. Woody Marks and Dare Ogunbowale will likely split backfield touches this week. The Texans used both Marks and Jawhar Jordan last week, but Jordan suffered an injured reserve-worthy injury. Marks should be in starting lineups, but he may be more of a FLEX than a reliable RB2. Ogunbowale is a low-floor PPR dart throw.

Source: Aaron Wilson

item.title: Chiefs placed Josh Simmons on injured reserve with a back injury.
item.description:
Josh Simmons KC Tackle

The Chiefs made head athletic trainer Rick Burkholder available to the media to explain the 2026 Simmons Saga today. On August 17th, the young left tackle reported calf discomfort in the same leg that he underwent a patellar tendon repair in 2024. Chiefs trainers discovered that a bulging, herniated disc in his lumbar spine was causing the lower-leg issue. According to Burkholder, offensive linemen occasionally deal with this type of disc issue, but Simmons’ issue was complicated because it was abnormally high up in the lumbar spine. Simmons consulted with a well-regarded spine specialist, who recommended rehabilitation instead of surgery. Imaging taken early in the rehab process showed improvement, so they stayed the course, but unfortunately, Simmons’ recovery has recently plateaued, leading to the injured reserve placement. Simmons will be eligible to return for the Chiefs’ Week 11 game against the Cardinals.

Source: Sam McDowell

item.title: CBS Sports’ Matt Zenitz reports Jeremiyah Love (ankle) is not expected to play in Week 7 against the Broncos.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Love didn’t practice on Wednesday after missing Week 6. It doesn’t sound like he will practice at all this week. Tyler Allgeier and Bam Knight will split the backfield again this week. Allgeier out-carried Knight 18-15 last week, but Knight was far more effective, running for 80 yards in total. Allgeier posted just 38 yards. He still figures to be the lead runner this week, but Allgeier shine as a plug-and-play RB2 is waning headed into Week 7.

Source: Matt Zenitz

item.title: Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Jordan Love (back) was “pretty beat up” after the Packers’ Week 6 win over the Cowboys.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

Love got checked out by the team’s chiropractor after the game and was listed as limited for yesterday’s practice. LaFleur told reporters they haven’t determined whether he will be limited for today’s session. Either way, he said yesterday that there is no chance Love misses Week 7, so the practice reports are a moot point. Love is a top-half QB1 for his date with Detroit this week.

Source: Weston Hodkiewicz

item.title: Matt LaFleur said he has no concerns about Christian Watson’s ankle injury ahead of the Packers’ Week 7 game against the Lions.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

The same is true of Matthew Golden, who is dealing with a shoulder issue. Both players were estimated as limited participants for Wednesday’s walkthrough. It doesn’t look like either wideout is at risk of missing the Packers’ upcoming shootout with Detroit. Watson is currently fifth in the league in receiving yards at 538. Golden is sixth at 501. Both players hold a spot in the WR1 ranks heading into Week 7.

Source: Weston Hodkiewicz

item.title: NFL Network’s Mike Garafolo reports Saquon Barkley (hamstring) is expected to return to practice today and “is in line to play Monday against the Cowboys.”
item.description:
Saquon Barkley PHI Running Back

Barkley will unfortunately return to a team without Jalen Hurts, but the Eagles’ offense is otherwise getting healthier ahead of a must-win matchup with the Cowboys. Barkley has been out since Week 4 because of the hamstring issue. Even in his first game back, we would expect Barkley to get the lion’s share of the backfield touches against a Dallas defense that is giving up the 10th-most fantasy points to running backs. Barkley would be, at worst, an RB2 for his Week 7 return.

Source: Mike Garafolo

item.title: Zach Charbonnet (knee) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Zach Charbonnet SEA Running Back

Charbonnet was expected to get a full week of practice, so this is no surprise. He is listed as a full participant for the first time since returning to practice and is trending to be activated off the physically unable to perform list ahead of a Week 7 matchup against the Chiefs. With Jadarian Price on injured reserve, he is headed for a sizeable share of the Seahawks’ ambiguous backfield. Charbonnet is in the RB3 ranks if activated.

item.title: Jordan Mason (thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jordan Mason MIN Running Back

Mason is firmly on track to play in Week 7 against the Colts. He should tentatively be expected to lead the backfield in carries right away, with Aaron Jones potentially settling into a 1B role. The Colts’ defense is not an imposing unit, so both running backs are FLEX-viable this week.

item.title: Brock Bowers (hamstring/calf) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Brock Bowers LV Tight End

Bowers is usually a limited practice participant due to his knee injury, before upgrading to full and eventually playing. However, this week is notable as he was listed with hamstring and calf injuries instead of a knee injury. He was still limited as usual on Wednesday but the new designations are something to keep an eye on throughout the week.

item.title: Mike Washington Jr. (foot/back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Mike Washington Jr. LV Running Back

In a semi-surprising twist of fate, the Raiders running back on the practice report with injuries is Washington, who was limited with foot and back injuries on Wednesday. Ashton Jeanty was not listed on the practice report. A limited practice indicates Washington is still trending to play Week 7, but with him appearing on the injury report and Jeanty off, any hopes for Washington achieving standalone fantasy value will have to wait.

item.title: Trent McDuffie (groin) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Trent McDuffie

McDuffie injured his groin during last Thursday’s practice and did not play in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He starts out this week not practicing, putting him on the wrong side of questionable for Week 7. Also not practicing was LB Nate Landman (concussion). The Rams defense continues to lose players to injury; the Raiders face this defense in Week 7 and could see more fruitful fantasy performances than usual.

item.title: Budda Baker (groin/illness) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Budda Baker ARI Safety

Baker played through the groin injury in Week 6 but starts out this week not practicing due to both the groin injury and an illness. Also not practicing for the Cardinals defense were DL Walter Nolen (ankle), S Andrew Wingard (knee), and CB Garrett Williams (knee). Each player will likely need to practice in some capacity in order to play in Week 7.

item.title: Jonah Elliss (leg) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jonah Elliss DEN Linebacker

Elliss suffered a lower-leg injury on his right leg in Week 6. Broncos head coach Sean Payton said Wednesday that the injury is not season-ending, but did not rule out a stint on injured reserve. Either way, it sounds like Elliss will miss Week 7 and potentially more.

Source: Zac Stevens

item.title: Christian Kirk (calf) was a full participant in Wednesday’s walkthrough practice.
item.description:
Christian Kirk SF Wide Receiver

Kirk was limited all of last week but starts out this week listed as a full participant for the 49ers’ Wednesday walkthrough practice. He remains on injured reserve, but head coach Kyle Shanahan said Kirk is a “possibility” for Week 7. A full practice listing is a good start and Kirk could see WR3 volume immediately with Mike Evans and Deebo Samuel dealing with injuries.

item.title: Jeremiyah Love (ankle) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Jeremiyah Love ARI Running Back

Love starts out not practicing for the second straight week due to an ankle injury. He missed Week 6 against the Rams and a DNP Wednesday puts him on the wrong side of questionable to play in Week 7 against the Broncos. Love will need to practice in some capacity to have a chance of playing this week, but Tyler Allgeier is back in the RB2 range if Love cannot go.

item.title: Tyler Badie (thumb) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Tyler Badie DEN Running Back

Badie was a non-participant in practice with a thumb injury. With Jonah Coleman designated to return from injured reserve, Badie does not need to be rostered for fantasy purposes.

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle briefly exited the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks before returning to the game. He now pops up on the practice report as a limited participant on Wednesday with a chest injury. Waddle is not in jeopardy of missing time just yet, but his poor fantasy production to start the season makes him a volatile fantasy option for Week 7 against the Cardinals.

item.title: Brian Robinson Jr. (hamstring) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Brian Robinson ATL Running Back

Robinson is the immediate backup to Bijan Robinson in the Falcons’ backfield, seeing his best usage in run-heavy game scripts. He was limited with a hamstring injury on Wednesday but is still trending to play Week 7 against the 49ers, barring setbacks. Also limited was Olamide Zaccheaus (shoulder). Both players are depth options at best behind the Falcons’ star-studded skill players.

item.title: Divine Deablo (forearm) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Divine Deablo ATL Linebacker

Deablo suffered a forearm injury in Week 6 and opens Week 7 not practicing. Also not practicing was CB Billy Bowman (hamstring). Both will need to practice in some capacity to play in Week 7 against the 49ers.

item.title: Kendal Daniels (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Kendal Daniels ATL Linebacker

Daniels was carted off the field on a stretcher in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears. It was a scary scene that paused the game for around fifteen minutes as Daniels’ neck was stabilized after he hit his head while attempting to make a tackle. Fortunately, the rookie appears to be okay as he appeared in practice as a full participant on Wednesday.

item.title: Rashid Shaheed (hip) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Rashid Shaheed SEA Wide Receiver

Shaheed was heavily involved in the Seahawks’ high-volume passing game in Week 6. He seemingly came out of the week banged-up and will open this week as a limited practice participant. Shaheed competes with Cooper Kupp for the No. 2 pass-catching role on the team but is only a boom-or-bust option for deep leagues at this point.

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Travis Kelce KC Tight End

Kelce played through an ankle issue in Week 6, catching five passes for 53 yards. Despite not playing at full health, he was still second on the team in targets. Kelce starts out the week as a limited practice participant and it would be a surprise if he misses National Tight End Day this week against the Seahawks.

item.title: TreVeyon Henderson (ankle) is not on the final injury report for Week 7 against the Bears.
item.description:
TreVeyon Henderson NE Running Back

Henderson will be active for the Patriots’ Thursday Night Football game, but his usage is up in the air. Patriots coach Mike Vrabel got RB Corey Kiner going late last week after Henderson fumbled. The Patriots won’t simply discard their former second-round pick, so he remains FLEX-viable, but he may be playing with a very limited touch count.

item.title: CJ Donaldson (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
CJ Donaldson NO Running Back

A limited practice to start the week is usually maintenance. Donaldson looked good last week, running for 39 yards on six attempts, though he did commit one fumble. Donaldson is one of three backs seeing work for the Saints, and none of them have made a strong case to get more touches. Donaldson is a weak FLEX option for Week 7.

item.title: Alvin Kamara (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Alvin Kamara NO Running Back

Kamara has been playing through the back issue for several weeks. He is expected to do so again this week. Kamara is part of a three-back committee, and he isn’t the leader of the trio, but that didn’t stop him from finding the end zone on nine touches last week. With a limited receiving role to go along with his shrinking rushing workload, he’s barely in the RB3 mix for Week 7.

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said the team is still determining “the best time” to schedule Davante Adams’ (hamstring) “cleanup” procedure.
item.description:
Davante Adams

Surgeries are sometimes delayed to help reduce swelling. Occasionally, new information is gathered during this time and/or during the surgery. Adams is currently expected to be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. Perhaps the wide return-to-play timeline is due to the fact that the surgeon has not yet fully assessed the injury. We tentatively expect the team to share an updated recovery timeline once Adams undergoes the procedure on his ruptured hamstring tendon. Stay tuned.

Source: Stu Jackson

item.title: Rico Dowdle (toe) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Rico Dowdle PIT Running Back

The Steelers will likely limit Dowdle’s reps for a few weeks as he manages the toe injury that cost him three games. He should be good to go for Sunday’s game by Friday. Dowdle saw 10 touches in his first game back and looked relatively explosive, running for 40 yards on seven attempts. He is in the RB3 mix for Week 7 versus the Saints.

item.title: Justin Jefferson (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Justin Jefferson MIN Wide Receiver

This is just a maintenance day for the Vikings’ No. 1 wide receiver. Jefferson has an excellent matchup this week against the struggling Colts’ defense. The unit will likely be without No. 1 CB Sauce Gardner (calf), further enhancing Jefferson’s WR1 outlook for Week 7.

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: Cam Jurgens (concussion) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Bengals.
item.description:
Cam Jurgens BAL Center

The Ravens acquired Jurgens from the Eagles two weeks ago, but he hasn’t made his Baltimore debut yet while he works through the league’s concussion protocol. A full practice today puts him on track to suit up in Week 7. His return will move rookie Vega Ioane back to right guard.

item.title: Jordan Addison (hamstring) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Colts.
item.description:
Jordan Addison MIN Wide Receiver

Addison, well-rested coming off his team’s Week 6 bye, is ready to go. The Colts’ defense has played poorly, and they will likely be without top CB Sauce Gardner (calf). Addison can be a volatile producer at times, but he warrants WR3/FLEX treatment this week.

Source: Minnesota Vikings

item.title: Rashod Bateman (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Rashod Bateman BAL Wide Receiver

Bateman left the Ravens’ Week 6 game against the Browns and did not return, though head coach Jesse Minter told reporters on Monday that he was going to be fine. Expect the team to manage his reps in practice this week with an eye on getting him ready for Sunday. Bateman has made a handful of splash plays this year, but his production is low-volume and high-variance. He will be a low-end FLEX option for Week 7.

item.title: Broncos designated Jonah Coleman (ankle) to return from injured reserve.
item.description:
Jonah Coleman DEN Running Back

Coleman can return to practice this week and the team now has 21 days to bring him off injured reserve. He could be back on the field as soon as Sunday. With the Broncos’ offense struggling and two backs already seeing work in the backfield, it’s hard to imagine Coleman having much fantasy value in his first game back. He’s worth stashing in deeper leagues, but it might be a while before fantasy managers want him in their lineups.

Source: James Palmer

item.title: Rams coach Sean McVay said the Rams have not had discussions about bringing in a receiver with Davante Adams (hamstring) sidelined for 6-10 weeks.
item.description:
Davante Adams

Earlier today, ESPN’s Dan Graziano reported that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.” Obviously, McVay doesn’t want to tip off other wide receiver-needy NFL teams about their potential entrance into the trade market, and he has no reason to be honest with us. Acquiring a new wide receiver makes sense, and the Rams were aggressive players in the trade market last offseason. Stay tuned.

Source: Adam Grosbard

item.title: ESPN’s Dan Graziano reports that the Rams “will at least explore the possibility of trading for a wide receiver.”
item.description:
Davante Adams

Adams is set to undergo a procedure after rupturing his hamstring tendon in Week 6 against the Cardinals. He will be sidelined for 6-10 weeks. The Rams were already very thin at wide receiver and Puka Nacua has spent multiple weeks on the injury report as well. Acquiring a capable wide receiver makes sense, but as Graziano mentions, the Rams have already traded away a lot of their draft capital. Thus far, GM Les Snead has already given up their 2027 first- and third-round picks, and their 2028 second-round pick and their 2029 third-round pick. He notes that Rams QB Stetson Bennett played for Browns coach Todd Monken in college. Perhaps Monken would be interested in a reunion.

Source: ESPN

item.title: Malik Willis (right thumb) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Jets.
item.description:
Malik Willis MIA Quarterback

ESPN’s Marcel Louis-Jacques reports that Willis received treatment for his thumb injury on his right, throwing hand, though he did not share what exactly the injury is. Hopefully, it is nothing serious. If his ball placement is impacted, the Jets’ D/ST would benefit. Willis is a volatile QB2 against them this week. Willis underwent surgery on his left thumb in August 2025.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: Jaylen Wright (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jaylen Wright MIA Running Back

The Dolphins’ speedy back will likely serve as a change-of-pace option behind Ollie Gordon, who has outplayed Wright since De’Von Achane’s season-ending knee injury. Wright does not need to be rostered in 12-team formats.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: Caleb Douglas (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Caleb Douglas MIA Wide Receiver

Douglas told reporters that he has finally progressed to being “day-to-day,” giving him a real chance to suit up in Week 7 against the Jets. Douglas should be added in 12-team formats. He played very well early on and will likely warrant FLEX consideration upon his return.

Source: Marcel Louis-Jacques

item.title: Pat Surtain (ankle) resumed practicing on Wednesday.
item.description:
Pat Surtain DEN Cornerback

NFL on Prime’s James Palmer reported last week that Surtain was likely to return for the Broncos’ Week 8 game against the Chiefs, rather than face the Cardinals in Week 7. Given Surtain’s multi-week absence, and Palmer’s reporting, we expect to see Surtain listed as a limited participant on the final injury report. Whether he returns in time for the Cardinals’ game remains to be seen.

Source: Mike Klis

item.title: Trent Brown (wrist) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Trent Brown HOU Tackle

Brown was on the injury report because of the wrist injury several times earlier in the season. The team only listed him with a knee issue last week, and he was cleared from the injury report on Friday, but it’s likely that he’s been managing the wrist injury all season. Blake Fisher, his projected backup, also missed practice today, so this is at least a situation to monitor throughout the week.

item.title: Dalton Schultz (quad) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Dalton Schultz HOU Tight End

Schultz never left the Texans’ Week 6 game against Jacksonville, but he was spotted with a limp after taking a knee to the leg. It’s possible the injury was worse than initially expected. If he were to miss Week 7, Foster Moreau, who scored twice last week, would be the next man up. Given that Schultz was barely putting up TE2 numbers as the starter, our hopes for Moreau as a streaming option would not be high.

item.title: Mike Evans (Achilles) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Mike Evans SF Wide Receiver

Evans is already expected to miss “a little time” because of his Achilles tendinitis, so this isn’t a surprise. It’s safe to assume he’s out for at least Week 7, but the good news is that it’s not expected to be a long-term issue. Evans could be back as soon as Week 9 following the 49ers’ bye week. With Deebo Samuel all but ruled out for this week’s matchup with Atlanta, Brandin Cooks and Jordan Watkins are set for starting roles on Sunday.

item.title: Falcons activated A.J. Terrell’s (groin) 21-day practice window from injured reserve.
item.description:
A.J. Terrell ATL Cornerback

Terrell was back on the practice field with his teammates today. He has a chance to face the 49ers and their banged-up wide receiver corps in Week 7. Terrell is a capable coverage defender. His return is a positive for the Falcons’ defense.

Source: Tori McElhaney

item.title: Darnell Mooney (neck) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Texans.
item.description:
Darnell Mooney NYG Wide Receiver

Mooney should be good to go this week, but he does not need to be on fantasy football rosters. Giants TE Theo Johnson (neck) was limited.

Source: Dan Salomone

item.title: Andrew Thomas (groin) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Andrew Thomas NYG Tackle

Thomas, the team’s left tackle, plus RT Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) and backup OT Marcus Mbow (knee) were all sidelined on Wednesday. Thomas played through a questionable tag last week. This unit is ailing. They face the Texans’ capable defensive line in Week 7.

Source: Jordan Raanan

item.title: Jevón Holland (concussion) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Jevón Holland NYG Safety

Holland, the team’s top safety, and Greg Newsome (concussion), the team’s top cornerback, were both sidelined today. Giants LB Tremaine Edmunds (shoulder) was also sidelined. The Giants are tasked with containing a Texans’ passing offense that ties for the league lead in explosive pass plays this week.

Source: New York Giants

item.title: Christian Watson (ankle) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Christian Watson GB Wide Receiver

The Packers held a walkthrough today, so Watson’s status is only an estimate from the team. Given his lengthy injury history, fantasy managers should keep an eye on Green Bay’s injury report tomorrow, though we suspect this isn’t a major issue for Watson. Assuming he gets up to a full practice at some point this week, Watson will be a borderline WR1 for Week 7 versus Detroit.

item.title: Matthew Golden (shoulder) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Matthew Golden GB Wide Receiver

A limited session this early in the week is usually nothing to worry about. After racking up another 100-yard game on Sunday, this time on 13 targets, Golden could use a little rest at practice. He was working his way into the WR1 ranks already, and a shootout with the Lions all but guarantees him a spot in the top 12 this week.

item.title: Carson Schwesinger (ankle) did not practice on Wednesday.
item.description:
Carson Schwesinger CLE Linebacker

This is probably just a maintenance day for the Browns’ linebacker. Schwesinger resumed practicing last Friday and ended up playing in Week 6 against the Ravens. We expect to see him resume practicing tomorrow. The Browns face the Titans in Week 7. Browns DT Mason Graham (knee/ankle) was limited.

Source: Cleveland Browns

item.title: Jordan Love (back) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jordan Love GB Quarterback

Wednesday’s session was a walkthrough, so this is just an estimate from the team. We don’t believe it will be much of an issue for Love in Week 7. Barring a setback, Love will remain in the QB1 mix for a likely shootout with the Lions on Sunday.

item.title: Dylan Sampson (knee) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Dylan Sampson CLE Running Back

Browns coach Todd Monken indicated earlier today that Sampson has a chance to return from injured reserve in time to face the Titans on Sunday. The Browns’ skill position corps is banged up and could use an explosive player. Sampson might end up warranting FLEX treatment right off the bat, if he is active this week.

Source: Daniel Oyefusi

item.title: Quinshon Judkins (ankle) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Quinshon Judkins CLE Running Back

Earlier today, Browns coach Todd Monken said he was “optimistic” about Judkins’ availability for Week 7 against the Titans. Today’s limited session puts him on track to play, though it would be nice to see him practice in full. If active, he would be a FLEX starter.

Source: Daniel Oyefusi

item.title: Nick Bosa (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Nick Bosa SF Defensive Lineman

Kyle Shanahan told reporters he’s hopeful Bosa returns to practice tomorrow. The oft-injured pass-rusher hasn’t played since Week 2. Even if he does practice on Thursday, there’s no guarantee that will get him back on the field for Sunday’s game against the Falcons.

Source: Matt Barrows

item.title: KC Concepcion (calf/quad) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
KC Concepcion KC Concepcion (calf/quad) was limited on Wednesday.

The rookie wide receiver has been awfully banged up over the past two weeks. He suffered a concussion in Week 5, yet managed to play in Week 6. Unfortunately, he did not leave the contest unscathed, picking up two lower-body injuries. Hopefully, he resumes practicing fully tomorrow.

Source: Daniel Oyefusi

item.title: Denzel Boston (foot) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Denzel Boston CLE Wide Receiver

Boston played through the injury last week, catching just 1-of-5 targets for 15 yards. The foot injury could be bugging him. Fortunately, he did not appear to suffer any setbacks. Boston is a WR3/FLEX against the Titans in Week 7.

Source: Daniel Oyefusi

item.title: Deebo Samuel (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Neither did Mike Evans, who is dealing with Achilles tendinitis. These absences shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. Evans is expected to miss Week 7 after aggravating his Achilles issue on Monday. Samuel is expected to miss “at least a couple of weeks” and has been sidelined for just one game so far. Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks are in line to start for the 49ers this week. What a time to be alive.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Calvin Ridley (hip) was limited on Wednesday.
item.description:
Calvin Ridley TEN Wide Receiver

The 31-year-old player has a hip injury. Ridley mostly runs cardio and game day and is not fantasy-relevant at this time. Were he to sit, Elic Ayomanor and Chimere Dike could get more playing time — which would be a positive outcome for the offense as a whole.

Source: Jim Wyatt

item.title: Luke Goedeke (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Luke Goedeke TB Tackle

The Bucs’ right tackle has not missed a snap this year. If he were to miss Week 7, Justin Skule would likely be the next man up. Goedeke has been an impressive pass protector this year, allowing seven pressures and zero sacks on 259 pass-pro reps. Losing him would be a notable blow to the team’s line.

item.title: A.J. Brown (ankle) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 7 against the Bears.
item.description:
A.J. Brown NE Wide Receiver

Brown practiced in full on Friday. It is his first time doing so since returning from injured reserve last week. This is great news for his Week 7 outlook. The Bears field a beatable pass defense, setting up Brown for a bounce-back performance after last week’s disappointing showing.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: Sean Tucker (quad) is practicing in full for Week 7 against the Panthers.
item.description:
Sean Tucker TB Running Back

Tucker should be back after missing Week 6’s loss to the Steelers. He doesn’t offer much fantasy value of his own, but he does occasionally plunder goal-line work from Bucky Irving. Expect him to be a thorn in Irving’s side again this week.

item.title: Baker Mayfield (thumb) practiced in full on Wednesday.
item.description:
Baker Mayfield TB Quarterback

Mayfield going down as a full participant is a bit of a surprise given that it’s his first time practicing in any capacity since Week 3. Todd Bowles told reporters earlier this week that the team was preparing for Jalon Daniels to start. Now it looks like Mayfield may be the favorite to draw the start versus Carolina. This is ultimately a rather ambiguous situation, likely by Bowles’ design. Fantasy managers should have a backup plan in place if they are counting on either of the Bucs’ quarterbacks this week.

item.title: Patriots ruled out Carlton Davis (neck) for Week 7 against the Bears.
item.description:
Carlton Davis NE Cornerback

The Patriots will also be without their top-two backup CBs, Karon Prunty (hamstring) and Channing Canada (hamstring). The Patriots listed S Kevin Byard (chest), S Craig Woodson (shoulder) and LB Christian Elliss (chest) as questionable. This is good news for the Bears’ passing attack.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: Patriots ruled out Alijah Vera-Tucker (hamstring) for Week 7 against the Bears.
item.description:
Alijah Vera-Tucker NE Guard

The Patriots will also be without RG Ben Brown (knee). The Bears’ defense is not an elite unit, but losing two starting guards is rough. Backups Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse will start instead. The Patriots listed RT Morgan Moses (foot) as questionable.

Source: New England Patriots

item.title: Kendal Daniels (neck) was a full participant in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Kendal Daniels ATL Linebacker

Daniels was carted off the field on a stretched in the Falcons’ Week 6 loss to the Bears. It was a scary scene that paused the game for around fifteen minutes as Daniels’ neck was stabilized after he hit his head while attempting to make a tackle. Fortunately, the rookie appears to be okay as he appeared in practice as a full participant on Wednesday.

item.title: Deebo Samuel (calf) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Deebo Samuel SF Wide Receiver

Neither did Mike Evans, who is dealing with Achilles tendinitis. These absences shouldn’t come as much of a surprise. Evans is expected to miss Week 8 after aggravating his Achilles issue on Monday. Samuel is expected to miss “at least a couple of weeks” and has been sidelined for just one game so far. Jordan Watkins and Brandin Cooks are in line to start for the 49ers this week. What a time to be alive.

Source: Nick Wagoner

item.title: Emeka Egbuka (concussion/foot) did not practice Wednesday.
item.description:
Emeka Egbuka TB Wide Receiver

Egbuka finished the Bucs’ overtime loss to the Steelers, so his concussion symptoms likely arose in the hours or days after the game. He will now need to pass through the league’s concussion protocol to be cleared for Week 7. Players typically miss one game while in the protocol, and we don’t know the severity of his foot injury. Fantasy managers should prepare to be without him for at least a week. His absence would free up more looks for Chris Godwin and rookie Ted Hurst, both of whom would be in the WR4 mix if Egbuka can’t go.

item.title: Jonah Jackson (hip/quad) is not on the final injury report for Week 7 against the Patriots.
item.description:
Jonah Jackson CHI Offensive Lineman

This is great news. Jackson is one of the best guards in football. Bears LB T.J. Edwards (hamstring) is doubtful, Jack Sanborn (concussion) has been ruled out, and CB Tyrique Stevenson (hip) is questionable.

Source: Chicago Bears

item.title: Bucky Irving (illness) did not practice Wednesay.
item.description:
Bucky Irving TB Running Back

Players missing time because of an illness this early in the weekend almost always get cleared to play by Sunday. We expect no difference from Irving. Coming off his third 20-touch game of the year, Irving remains a high-end RB2 for his Week 7 date with the Panthers.

item.title: Ravens coach Jesse Minter said Lamar Jackson (ankle) got in “a little bit of limited work” during Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Lamar Jackson BAL Quarterback

Jackson was not spotted during the portion of practice open to the media but apparently participated in some capacity later in the session. It’s a step in the right direction, but Jackson likely still has several hurdles to clear before returning to action. Despite Minter’s comments, we expect Jackson to miss another week. Tyler Huntley will draw the start versus Cincinnati if Jackson is ruled out.

Source: Ian Rapoport

item.title: Jaylen Waddle (chest) was limited in Wednesday’s practice.
item.description:
Jaylen Waddle DEN Wide Receiver

Waddle briefly exited the Broncos’ Week 6 win over the Seahawks before returning to the game. He now pops up on the practice reported as a limited participant on Wednesday with a chest injury. Waddle is not in jeopardy of missing time just yet, but his poor fantasy production to start the season makes him a volatile fantasy option for Week 7 against the Cardinals.
